parts.visual:
A founder spends 2 years and $1 Million building the 'perfect' software in secret. They launch it. Nobody wants it. They are bankrupt.

The Antidote:
1. The MVP (Minimum Viable Product): A version of a new product which allows a team to collect the maximum amount of validated learning about customers with the least effort.
2. The Core Rule: If you are not embarrassed by the first version of your product, you launched too late.
parts.audio: The MVP is not a broken product; it is the absolute smallest thing you can build to test if your core hypothesis is true. Do not waste years building features nobody asked for.

questions.question: A founder wants to build an app that uses AI to write legal contracts. Building the AI will take a year. What is the best MVP to test the market *this week*?
options: Wait a year and build the AI.

Create a simple landing page that says 'AI Legal Contracts - $50'. When a customer pays, the founder manually writes the contract themselves and emails it. This proves people will actually pay for the service before writing any code.
Write a blog post about AI.
questions.correct_answer: Create a simple landing page that says 'AI Legal Contracts - $50'. When a customer pays, the founder manually writes the contract themselves and emails it. This proves people will actually pay for the service before writing any code.
questions.explanation: This is known as the 'Wizard of Oz' MVP. It looks automated on the outside, but is manual on the inside.

questions.question: Listen to the engineer complaining about the MVP. Why is the founder ignoring him?
questions.tts_text: The design looks terrible! It only has two buttons! The database isn't scalable! We can't let users see this, it will ruin our reputation!
options: The engineer is obsessed with perfection, but the founder knows the MVP is only a tool for 'Validated Learning'. The goal is to get user feedback immediately, not to win a design award.
questions.correct_answer: The engineer is obsessed with perfection, but the founder knows the MVP is only a tool for 'Validated Learning'. The goal is to get user feedback immediately, not to win a design award.
questions.explanation: Perfect is the enemy of shipped.

questions.question: What is the danger of asking your friends 'Is this a good idea?' instead of building an MVP?
options: Friends will lie to you to protect your feelings. An MVP forces real customers to vote with their credit cards, which is the only data that actually matters.
questions.correct_answer: Friends will lie to you to protect your feelings. An MVP forces real customers to vote with their credit cards, which is the only data that actually matters.
questions.explanation: A verbal 'yes' is worthless. A credit card transaction is truth.

questions.question: What does a startup do *after* launching the MVP and collecting data?
options: They execute the 'Build-Measure-Learn' feedback loop. If the data shows the idea is wrong, they execute a 'Pivot' (a fundamental change in strategy) instead of blindly continuing to fail.
questions.correct_answer: They execute the 'Build-Measure-Learn' feedback loop. If the data shows the idea is wrong, they execute a 'Pivot' (a fundamental change in strategy) instead of blindly continuing to fail.
questions.explanation: Startups are essentially high-speed science experiments.

pairs.match: Minimum Viable Product (the simplest version of a product that can be released)
A structured course correction designed to test a new fundamental hypothesis about the product
A product that appears fully functional to the user but is operated manually behind the scenes
A process in which one learns by trying out an initial idea and then measuring it to substantiate the effect
